questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY
questions.topic: Language change, contact, and social meaning
questions.learningObjective: examine language change using anthropological evidence

stimulus.body: A comparison of texts separated by centuries shows that a language's sounds, words, and grammar have all shifted gradually.

questions.stem: Which statement about language change is best supported by the account?

options.text: Language change is the alteration of a language's structure and vocabulary over time as it is transmitted between generations.
Language change is a sudden replacement of a language by an unrelated one in a single year.
options.misconception: The comparison shows gradual shifts across sounds, words, and grammar.

options.text: Language change occurs only when a written standard is formally revised by an academy.
options.misconception: It imagines a sudden event, whereas change is normally gradual and continuous.

options.text: Language change can be observed only in languages that have no written form.
options.misconception: It limits change to official revision, whereas spoken change happens constantly.

questions.explanation: It wrongly requires the absence of writing, when written records are valuable evidence.
questions.hint: All living languages change continuously, whether or not speakers notice.

questions.learningObjective: examine sound change using anthropological evidence

questions.stem: The evidence most strongly supports which claim about sound change?

options.text: Sound change is a single speaker's temporary lisp that disappears after therapy.
options.misconception: The loss of final consonants affected an entire class of words systematically.

options.text: Sound change is a systematic alteration in the pronunciation of a language over time, often affecting whole classes of words.

options.text: Sound change is the borrowing of a word from a neighbouring language.

questions.hint: Sound changes are regular and affect all eligible words in a given environment.

questions.learningObjective: examine semantic change using anthropological evidence

questions.stem: Which choice correctly identifies semantic change in this case?
